metadata.icdo_version: ICD-O-3.2. morphology_entries[] is GENERATED by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group V from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite, never transcribed from an option file or a diagnostic pathway document (Group 5 build contract Sec.1). Two codes on this stem are absent from this file, and neither absence is a deletion: 9510/0 Retinocytoma exists and is current in ICD-O-3.2 but is coded at behaviour 0, outside ICCC-3 Group V's behaviour-3 declaration (contract Sec.0.2, Sec.2.1); 9514/1 Retinoblastoma, spontaneously regressed exists and is current in ICD-O-3.2 at behaviour 1 only — ICD-O-3.2 carries no 9514/3 — and is likewise outside the declaration (contract Sec.0.2, Sec.2.2). The generator's own summary line records codes_absent_from_icdo32: ['9514'], meaning ICD-O-3.2 carries no 9514/3, not that 9514 is missing from ICD-O-3.2 altogether — the identical mechanism that kept 8683 out of Group IV (Group 4 contract Sec.0.2). Both codes are recorded only inside a behaviour_exclusion block in this file (rb_enucleation_report, rb_retinocytoma_word), never as a morphology_code. All four IARC 3.1-to-3.2 change documents were searched for '951[0-9]', 'retinoblast', 'retinocyt' and 'retinom' on 22 September 2026: no hits in any of the four, so this stem predates ICD-O-3.2 and was untouched by it (contract Sec.0.3).

morphology_entries.imaging_features: A calcified intraocular mass on B-scan ultrasound (or, when unavailable, orbital magnetic resonance imaging, which detects calcification poorly) in a child under five years, with no feature suggesting a leukocoria mimic. Razek & Elkhamary 2011; Ghose & Kaliki 2022; College of American Pathologists Retinoblastoma Protocol v4.0.0.0, Note A (build contract Sec.0.5). Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05, names retinoblastoma as one of only five entities in the entire European Network of Cancer Registries scheme registrable at basis 1 (clinical examination alone) or basis 2 (clinical investigation, including imaging) with no tissue at all, topography C69.2, morphology 9510/3.
morphology_entries.coding_note: Generated by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group V from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite, never transcribed (build contract Sec.1). Preferred term 'Retinoblastoma, NOS', behaviour 3, confirmed in icdo32.sqlite with no [obs] marker and no see_also / see_note / includes / excludes on the stem (contract Sec.0.3). This is the dominant, modal code in the group: most retinoblastoma cases in this registry will code 9510/3, because biopsy of an intact globe is contraindicated and diagnosis is ordinarily clinical plus imaging (contract Sec.0.5). Milman T, Grossniklaus HE, Goldman-Levy G, et al. The 5th Edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Tumours of the Eye and Orbit. Ocular Oncology and Pathology 2023;9(3-4):71-95 [the copy held is the online-first version, paginated 1-25, not the bound 71-95 print pagination -- contract Sec.10.2b], Table 9, Tumours of the neurosensory retina, lists Retinoblastoma as one of four named entities -- confirming a current World Health Organization entity lives on this stem. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05: Retinoblastoma is basis 1 or 2, topography C69.2, morphology 9510/3 (contract Sec.0.4). No branch in this tree may reach 9511, 9512 or 9513 without a pathology report; every basis-1 and basis-2 terminal emits 9510/3 only. who_version is recorded as 'WHO 2023', the year of the paper that classifies and names the entity on this stem, not the year the entity's behaviour was first fixed. The bound WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th edition, Volume 13: Eye and Orbit Tumours (IARC, ISBN 978-92-832-4546-9) did not reach final print until 23 January 2026, thirty-three months after the April 2023 online-first beta this paper summarises, and no published comparison of the two exists -- whether the retina chapter changed between them is not established (contract Sec.10.2, registrar item Sec.11.7). code_neutral_molecular is true: RB1 germline status, MYCN amplification and chromosome 6p gain drive counselling and prognosis, not the code -- hereditary and sporadic retinoblastoma both code 9510/3 (contract Sec.0.5, fact 3). CORRECTED 2026-09-22 by the build controller. This entry previously declared diagnostic_tests_required ['Histology']. 9510 is the imaging-sufficient code and is reached with no tissue on the modal path, so the engine computed Histology as an OUTSTANDING test and wrote its own upgrade sentence, 'Histology would yield a more specific code.', onto a case with an intact globe — inviting a contraindicated procedure and misreporting the case as incompletely worked up. Build contract Sec.5.4 maps examination under anaesthesia, ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging all onto 'Imaging'; Sec.5.5 bans the missing-test framing outright. upgrade_path is authored so app.js's automatic sentence (app.js outcome assembly, `auto`) never fires on any 9510 terminal.
morphology_entries.upgrade_path: The only more specific codes in this group — 9511 differentiated, 9512 undifferentiated, 9513 diffuse — are read off an enucleation or exenteration pathology report. Enucleation is a TREATMENT decision, not an outstanding investigation: biopsy of an eye that still contains the tumour is contraindicated and risks spreading it outside the eye. Do not record this case as incompletely worked up because no histology exists, and do not request tissue on account of this code.

morphology_entries.coding_note: Generated by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group V (contract Sec.1). Preferred term 'Retinoblastoma, differentiated', behaviour 3, a live, non-obsolete term in icdo32.sqlite, untouched by all four IARC 3.1-to-3.2 change documents (contract Sec.0.3). Milman T, et al. Ocular Oncology and Pathology 2023;9(3-4):71-95 [online-first copy held, paginated 1-25 -- contract Sec.10.2b], Table 9, lists exactly four entities under Tumours of the neurosensory retina -- Astrocytic tumours, Nodular and massive retinal gliosis, Retinocytoma, Retinoblastoma -- and names no separate 'differentiated' or 'undifferentiated' type. The paper's own Table 2 defines Type, Subtype and Pattern, and its Table 1 shows Subtypes are a subsection inside an entity's own section, not an entry in the chapter's type list -- so Table 9's silence shows only that this is not a separate type; it says nothing about whether a World Health Organization subtype carrying its own ICD-O code sits inside the Retinoblastoma entity page, which is paywalled and was not read (contract Sec.10.3). The paper states no ICD-O code anywhere in twenty-five pages (contract Sec.10.2b) -- a paper that prints no code cannot retire one. This code is therefore retained -- ICD-O-3.2 prints it as a live, non-obsolete Preferred term and it is a REDCap option -- and reachable only from the pathology report's own stated differentiation grade or growth pattern, the Group 4 D3 precedent on comparable evidence (contract Sec.2.4, Sec.10.3). who_version is recorded as 'ICD-O-3.2', not a World Health Organization edition: no current World Health Organization entity has been confirmed on this stem (registrar item Sec.11.5). Mapping, from the College of American Pathologists Retinoblastoma Protocol v4.0.0.0 (2017) and contract Sec.2.4: fleurette formation or neuronal differentiation (grade G1); numerous Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes, moderately differentiated (grade G2); or, on Mendoza's anaplasia scale (Mendoza PR, et al. Histopathologic grading of anaplasia in retinoblastoma. American Journal of Ophthalmology 2015;159(4):764-776), a retinocytoma-grade area or mild anaplasia recorded within an otherwise viable retinoblastoma -- not a standalone retinocytoma, which is 9510/0 and behaviour-excluded (contract Sec.2.1, Sec.2.3). code_neutral_molecular is true (contract Sec.0.5).

Generated by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group V (contract Sec.1). Preferred term 'Retinoblastoma, undifferentiated', behaviour 3, a live, non-obsolete term in icdo32.sqlite (contract Sec.0.3). Milman 2023 Table 9 names no separate 'undifferentiated' type on the retinoblastoma stem (see the 9511 entry's coding_note for the full reasoning; it applies identically here). The paper prints no ICD-O code anywhere, so it cannot retire one (contract Sec.10.2b); the code is retained on ICD-O-3.2's own authority and reachable only from the pathology report's own stated wording (contract Sec.2.4). who_version recorded as 'ICD-O-3.2': no current World Health Organization entity has been confirmed on this stem (registrar item Sec.11.5). Mapping, from the College of American Pathologists Retinoblastoma Protocol v4.0.0.0 (2017) and contract Sec.2.4: occasional rosettes, poorly differentiated (grade G3); no rosettes present, anaplasia, poorly differentiated (grade G4); or, on Mendoza's anaplasia scale (Mendoza PR, et al. American Journal of Ophthalmology 2015;159(4):764-776), severe anaplasia. Mendoza 2015 also records that severe anaplasia independently flags metastatic risk even with no standard high-risk histopathological feature present -- a clinical consequence, not a coding one, and recorded in docs/clinical-warnings.md, not here (contract Sec.9). code_neutral_molecular is true (contract Sec.0.5).

Generated by build/generate_group_inventory.py --group V (contract Sec.1). Preferred term 'Retinoblastoma, diffuse', behaviour 3, a live, non-obsolete term in icdo32.sqlite (contract Sec.0.3). Milman 2023 Table 9 names no separate 'diffuse' type on the retinoblastoma stem; growth pattern (endophytic, exophytic, mixed, diffuse infiltrating) most likely sits at the paper's own Table 2 third level, pattern, below subtype -- not established either way, since the entity page that would confirm it is paywalled (contract Sec.10.3). The code is retained on ICD-O-3.2's own authority and reachable only from the enucleation report's own stated growth pattern (contract Sec.2.4). who_version recorded as 'ICD-O-3.2': no current World Health Organization entity has been confirmed on this stem (registrar item Sec.11.5). imaging_sufficient is false here and false nowhere else matters as much: diffuse infiltrating retinoblastoma grows as a flat placoid infiltrate without a discrete calcified mass, is rare, presents later (around age six), and mimics uveitis or endophthalmitis, so the imaging-pathway's own calcified-mass and under-five criteria would falsely exclude it (contract Sec.2.5) -- this code is enucleation-only. code_neutral_molecular is true (contract Sec.0.5).

decision_trees.tree_label: Retinoblastoma (C69.0-C69.9 eye and adnexa; ICCC-3 Group V declares behaviour 3 at any site) — the imaging-first pathway, cytology and liquid biopsy, and the enucleation/exenteration report's own subtype wording

nodes.question: A child with a suspected retinal tumour (retinoblastoma). What is actually in this patient's file?
nodes.hint: Biopsy of an eye that still contains the tumour is avoided, because incisional or needle biopsy risks seeding the tumour outside the eye. A pathology report therefore exists only once the eye itself has been removed as treatment. B-scan ultrasound and orbital magnetic resonance imaging are not available everywhere, so the next step records which imaging was actually performed.
nodes.coding_note: Tree architecture per build contract Sec.4: five routes off this node. The contract's own diagram lists the fifth route's (inadequate/uninterpretable specimen) destination as 'rb_imaging_pathway or the non-registrable terminal' without deciding between them. This build routes it to rb_imaging_pathway: a failed tissue attempt does not erase whatever clinical/imaging evidence is also in the file, so that evidence is checked against the full constellation before the case falls through the pathway's own insufficient_next_node (rb_imaging_insufficient) to a non-reportable or Group XII outcome. Recorded for the registrar as a judgement call, per verification instructions.

options.label: Referral letter or clinical note only — no ophthalmic examination or imaging report, no cytology, no pathology report in the file
Ophthalmic examination under anaesthesia, B-scan ultrasound, and/or orbital magnetic resonance imaging report — the eye is intact, no cytology, no pathology report
Cytology report, or an aqueous-humour or plasma liquid biopsy report — no enucleation or exenteration specimen in the file
Enucleation or exenteration specimen with a pathology report
A specimen (cytology, or enucleation/exenteration) was obtained but is reported INADEQUATE, non-diagnostic, or technically UNINTERPRETABLE

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: This is the only clinical-alias node in the tool that emits a specific code on wording alone. Recorded only when cancer is at least likely on the note's own words -- not merely possible, and not when a non-malignant cause could equally explain the findings.
nodes.coding_note: Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05: retinoblastoma is one of only five entities in the entire European Network of Cancer Registries scheme registrable at basis 1, clinical examination alone, with no imaging and no tissue (build contract Sec.0.4, Sec.4). Basis 1 is legal here specifically because it is guarded by group in the validator and Table 3 names retinoblastoma's row '1 or 2' -- the ban that applies to Group 3 does not apply to Group 5 (contract Sec.0.6). Rule 4, p. 03: 'possible is not registrable' -- if clinical investigation makes cancer only possible, or a non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings, the case is not registered at all in the absence of pathology; this is a non_reportable destination, not a refer_group one, because Coats disease and persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous are not cancers in any group (contract Sec.0.4 point 4).

options.label: Note states retinoblastoma, or describes leukocoria (white pupillary reflex, or 'cat's-eye reflex') or strabismus with a suspected intraocular tumour of the retina
options.reason: Retinoblastoma is one of only five entities in the entire European Network of Cancer Registries scheme that may be registered on clinical examination alone, with no imaging and no tissue (Visser O, et al., Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05). Recorded as Retinoblastoma, NOS (9510/3) at basis of diagnosis 1.

options.label: Note describes a mass, a red-reflex abnormality, or 'for eye examination' with no diagnosis asserted — or the differential named includes a non-malignant cause (for example Coats disease or persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous) that could equally explain the findings
options.reason: Cancer is only possible, not at least likely, on the note's own wording, or a non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings. Under Visser 2023 rule 4 (p. 03), this is not registered at all in the absence of pathology.

nodes.question: No tissue exists. Tick every feature the ophthalmic examination and imaging report actually state, then answer the diversion checklist below.
nodes.hint: Feature 2, calcification within the mass, is the discriminator and is not optional. Leukocoria causes retinoblastoma in only 56-72% of children; the rest is Coats disease, persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous, coloboma, sclerosing endophthalmitis, retinal astrocytoma, Norrie disease, retinopathy of prematurity and medulloepithelioma (Razek & Elkhamary 2011), and those mimics characteristically show no calcified mass. Ultrasound, not magnetic resonance imaging, is the calcification detector -- magnetic resonance imaging detects calcification poorly, and computed tomography is avoided in a child who may carry a germline tumour-suppressor mutation. Record whichever imaging was actually performed; B-scan ultrasound and orbital magnetic resonance imaging are not available everywhere, and that is a reason to record what was done, not a reason to withhold this route.
nodes.coding_note: Engine constraint (build contract Sec.0.6, docs/TODO.md Sec.10): imagingPathway() renders only imaging_features, biochemical_questions and diversion_criteria -- options[] is never rendered. This node therefore declares insufficient_next_node, does not declare options[], and carries its own morphology_code/behavior_code/basis_of_diagnosis for the confirmed-constellation outcome. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 3, pp. 04-05: retinoblastoma is basis 2 on clinical investigation (imaging) with no tissue -- the modal output of the whole group (contract Sec.0.4 point 2). Diversion criteria per contract Sec.4.1: two patterns (no calcified mass; anterior-segment/inflammatory picture) point to a non-malignant mimic and are not registered without pathology (Visser rule 4, p. 03); two patterns (diffuse-infiltrating/older child; extraocular or orbital extension) still need tissue and must not be read as 'not cancer' (contract Sec.2.5, Sec.4.1) -- rb_imaging_insufficient carries that distinction forward.
imaging_features: An intraocular mass on B-scan ultrasound or on orbital magnetic resonance imaging
Calcification within the mass — on ultrasound, high-reflectivity foci casting acoustic shadows
Child under five years of age

diversion_criteria.feature: Retinal detachment or exudate with no calcified mass
diversion_criteria.reason: Matches the Coats disease or persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous pattern rather than retinoblastoma. A non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings, and under Visser 2023 rule 4 (p. 03) the case is not registered without pathology.

diversion_criteria.feature: A flat, diffusely infiltrating intraocular process with no discrete mass, or a child aged five years or older
diversion_criteria.reason: Matches diffuse infiltrating retinoblastoma, which grows without a discrete calcified mass and presents later than typical retinoblastoma. The calcified-mass and under-five criteria above would wrongly exclude it. This constellation needs tissue, not exclusion.

Suggests an inflammatory mimic such as endophthalmitis or uveitis. A non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings, and under Visser 2023 rule 4 (p. 03) the case is not registered without pathology.

Changes the specimen that will arrive — an exenteration rather than a straightforward enucleation, or treatment before any specimen exists — so the case is directed to await that tissue rather than registered on imaging alone.

nodes.step_label: Imaging did not confirm — what next
nodes.question: The imaging constellation did not confirm retinoblastoma — either a diversion criterion applies or a required feature is missing. What does the file show?
nodes.hint: The diversion criteria are not equivalent. A non-calcified pattern, or an anterior-segment/inflammatory picture, points to a mimic and is not registered without pathology. A diffuse infiltrating pattern, an older child, or extraocular extension is still a real possibility of retinoblastoma that needs tissue, not exclusion.
nodes.coding_note: Reached only from rb_imaging_pathway's insufficient_next_node. Build contract Sec.4.1: the diversion criteria send a case to tissue, which is the correct outcome, not to a 'not cancer' terminal — so the diffuse-variant/older-child and extraocular-extension patterns route to refer_group 12 (an honest 'pending tissue' state), never to non_reportable. The non-calcified and anterior-segment/inflammatory patterns are the genuine Visser rule 4 case (p. 03): a non-malignant disorder could equally explain the findings, so the case is not registered without pathology. Options 3 and 4 exist because tissue can arrive after an imaging attempt was already made.

options.label: Findings match a non-malignant mimic — retinal detachment or exudate with no calcified mass (Coats disease / persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous pattern), or an anterior-segment/inflammatory picture (pseudohypopyon) — and no tissue is in the file
options.reason: A non-malignant disorder could equally explain these findings. Under Visser 2023 rule 4 (p. 03), the case is not registered at all in the absence of pathology.

options.label: Findings match the diffuse variant (a flat, diffusely infiltrating process with no discrete mass, or a child aged five or older), or show extraocular or orbital extension — no tissue yet obtained
options.reason: This cannot be registered as Retinoblastoma, NOS on the imaging constellation alone — a diffuse infiltrating growth pattern, an older child, or extraocular extension all need a tissue diagnosis rather than exclusion. Record it provisionally under Group XII (8000/3, malignant neoplasm, NOS) pending cytology, a liquid biopsy, or an enucleation/exenteration specimen.

options.label: Tissue has since been obtained — a cytology or liquid-biopsy report is now in the file
Tissue has since been obtained — an enucleation or exenteration specimen with a pathology report is now in the file

nodes.question: What does the cytology or liquid-biopsy report show?
nodes.hint: Biopsy of an intact globe is avoided because of the risk of extraocular seeding; this option exists only because the report may already be in the file, not as a route to seek out. Diagnostic features of malignancy — necrosis, mitoses and nuclear atypia — should be present before retinoblastoma is diagnosed on a cytology. Sampling of retinal neurons and scant material are the two pitfalls that can mislead a cytological read; consultation with an experienced ophthalmic cytopathologist is recommended when a biopsy is considered. A cytology cannot grade differentiation or establish a growth pattern, so it never yields a subtype.
nodes.coding_note: Added once the baseline paper was on disk (build contract Sec.4, Sec.10.9). Milman T, et al. Ocular Oncology and Pathology 2023;9(3-4):71-95 [online-first copy held, paginated 1-25], Table 10, Diagnostic cytology of tumours of the retina and neuroepithelium, verbatim: 'Generally, biopsy is avoided due to the risk of extraocular recurrence and metastasis. Cytological samples often have pitfalls (sampling of retinal neurons, scant material) that may be misleading. Diagnostic features of malignancy such as necrosis, mitoses, and nuclear atypia should be present when diagnosing retinoblastoma in a cytology. Consultation with an experienced ophthalmic cytopathologist is recommended if a biopsy is considered.' Read carefully: avoided, with conditions attached for when it is done, not never done. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, Table 1 (p. 03): cytology is basis 5, stronger than the imaging route's basis 2. Rule 8, p. 06: an aqueous-humour or plasma liquid biopsy is basis 5 as well, not 8, whenever no pathology is available, even when it finds a cancer-specific genetic abnormality. 'Cytology' is used here as the evidence_tests tag; the closed diagnostic_tests_required vocabulary on morphology_entries[] (Referral only / Histology / Imaging / IHC / ISH / Flow cytometry / Cytogenetics-FISH / Molecular-PCR) has no literal cytology entry, so morphology_entries[9510].diagnostic_tests_required is left at ['Histology'] and this branch-level tag is a free-form tracking value, not a closed-list field.

options.label: Cytology or liquid biopsy shows malignant cells consistent with retinoblastoma, with necrosis, mitoses and/or nuclear atypia present
options.reason: Cells consistent with retinoblastoma are present on cytology, at European Network of Cancer Registries basis of diagnosis 5. A cytology cannot grade differentiation or establish a growth pattern, so this is recorded as Retinoblastoma, NOS (9510/3), never a subtype.
options.coding_note: satisfies_tests ['Imaging'] added 2026-09-22: a cytology or liquid-biopsy report is ENCR basis 5, above the basis 2 the imaging constellation carries (Visser 2023, Table 1). Imaging is not an outstanding test on a case that already has cells, and leaving it outstanding would have printed 'Imaging would yield a more specific code.' — which is untrue: imaging yields no more specific code in this group at all.

options.label: Cytology or liquid biopsy is non-diagnostic, shows scant material or sampled retinal neurons only, or the diagnostic features of malignancy (necrosis, mitoses, nuclear atypia) are not present
options.reason: The cytology or liquid biopsy did not show the diagnostic features of malignancy, or yielded only scant material or sampled retinal neurons. This cannot be registered as Retinoblastoma, NOS. Record it provisionally under Group XII (8000/3, malignant neoplasm, NOS) pending a diagnostic specimen — an enucleation or exenteration report, or a repeat liquid biopsy.

nodes.question: What does the enucleation or exenteration pathology report state about the tumour's differentiation, growth pattern, or anaplasia?
nodes.hint: Code from the report's own stated wording — do not infer a grade or growth pattern yourself. Where the report gives a differentiation grade, use it. Where it gives a Mendoza anaplasia grade instead, retinocytoma-grade or mild anaplasia sits at the differentiated end and severe anaplasia at the undifferentiated end. Where the report states more than one grade, code the higher. Severe anaplasia outranks a G1 or G2 differentiation grade, and a G3 or G4 differentiation grade outranks mild anaplasia. Moderate anaplasia changes no code where a differentiation grade is stated. Where the report also states a diffuse infiltrating growth pattern, code diffuse (9513), the higher code. Enucleation is the treatment that produced this specimen, not an outstanding investigation — nothing further needs to be removed from the child to read a fuller report on tissue already in hand.
nodes.coding_note: Mapping per College of American Pathologists Retinoblastoma Protocol v4.0.0.0 (2017) and build contract Sec.2.4. Where a report states more than one grade the higher governs (registrar's decision, 7 October 2026): the WHO ICD-O-3 first revision, section 4.3.4, pp. 21-22, assigns the higher of two stated degrees and sets 'anaplastic' at grade IV beside 'undifferentiated'; the College of American Pathologists protocol, p. 4, and Mendoza 2015, p. 765, grade anaplasia on its highest level in the tumour. Severe anaplasia therefore outranks G1 and G2. Moderate anaplasia alone stays unresolved, as below. A stated diffuse infiltrating growth pattern outranks a grade because 9513 is the higher code (Rule K; registrar's decision, 7 October 2026). Mendoza bridge: 'Where the report states a Mendoza anaplasia grade instead of a differentiation grade, the bridge is: retinocytoma-grade or mild ~ the differentiated end; severe ~ the undifferentiated end' (contract Sec.2.4). The contract does not state where a report giving moderate anaplasia alone (no differentiation grade, and not severe) should fall; this build folds that case into the GX/9510 option as the conservative, least-specific default, rather than guessing toward 9511 or 9512 — flagged here for the registrar, not resolved. Mendoza PR, et al. American Journal of Ophthalmology 2015;159(4):764-776 defines the scale. The retinocytoma homonym (contract Sec.2.3) is not resolved on this node: any report using the word 'retinocytoma' or 'retinoma' routes to rb_retinocytoma_word, which asks whether the word names a standalone lesion or an area of differentiation inside an active retinoblastoma, in the report's own words, and does not infer.

options.label: Diffuse infiltrating growth — the tumour spreads laterally within the retina with no discrete mass

Fleurette formation or neuronal differentiation (grade G1); numerous Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes, moderately differentiated (grade G2); or, on the Mendoza anaplasia scale, a retinocytoma-grade area or mild anaplasia recorded within an otherwise viable retinoblastoma; and no poorer grade or severe anaplasia stated

Occasional rosettes, poorly differentiated (grade G3); no rosettes present, anaplasia, poorly differentiated (grade G4); or, on the Mendoza anaplasia scale, severe anaplasia (also where a G1 or G2 grade is stated beside it)
Enucleation performed; the report states no differentiation grade and no growth pattern (grade GX) — or states only moderate anaplasia on the Mendoza scale with no differentiation grade given
options.reason: The enucleation specimen confirms retinoblastoma, but the report states no differentiation grade and no growth pattern. Recorded as Retinoblastoma, NOS (9510/3). A fuller reading of the same specimen stating a grade or growth pattern would allow this case to move to a specific subtype; nothing further needs to be removed from the child to get that detail.
options.coding_note: satisfies_tests ['Imaging'] added 2026-09-22: the enucleation specimen is ENCR basis 7 and settles the diagnosis. Imaging is not outstanding on an eye that has been removed.

options.label: The report uses the word 'retinocytoma' or 'retinoma' anywhere in its description
The report describes a shrunken, calcified, non-functional globe (phthisis bulbi) with no viable tumour — consistent with spontaneous regression

behaviour_exclusion.reason: A spontaneously regressed retinoblastoma is the shrunken, calcified, non-functional globe (phthisis bulbi) with no viable tumour. ICD-O-3.2 codes it 9514/1. ICCC-3 Group V admits behaviour 3 only, so it is not a registrable cancer in this group and no Group V code is emitted for it. Whether the registry registers a regressed retinoblastoma as an incident case, and on what code, is a registration-rules question for the registrar, not a morphology question this tool can settle. Record the finding and refer the case to the registrar.

nodes.question: The enucleation or exenteration report uses the word 'retinocytoma' or 'retinoma'. What does the report actually describe?
nodes.hint: 'Retinocytoma' names two different things and only the report's own wording can decide which: a standalone benign lesion with no viable retinoblastoma anywhere in the specimen, or an area of differentiation — the lowest grade on Mendoza's anaplasia scale — inside an otherwise active, malignant retinoblastoma. Read what the rest of the report says about the specimen as a whole; do not infer from the word alone. If the report also states a diffuse infiltrating growth pattern, choose the diffuse option: a growth pattern outranks a grade.
nodes.coding_note: Build contract Sec.2.3: coding a retinocytomatous area within an active retinoblastoma as 9510/0 would record a benign tumour for a child who has a malignant one. Mendoza PR, et al. American Journal of Ophthalmology 2015;159(4):764-776 runs the anaplasia scale retinocytoma/mild/moderate/severe inside an active retinoblastoma. Al-Hussaini M, Al Sharie S, Sultan H, Mohammad M, Yousef YA. Retinocytoma: understanding pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment approaches. International Journal of Retina and Vitreous 2025;11:20, confirms 9510/0 as the ICD-O code for standalone retinocytoma. Milman 2023 records that the World Health Organization classifies retinocytoma as premalignant on genetic and clinical grounds (biallelic RB1 mutations; can dedifferentiate into retinoblastoma), while ICD-O-3.2 codes it 9510/0, behaviour 0 (benign) — the behaviour code is IARC's, not the World Health Organization's, and the tool codes to ICD-O-3.2 (contract Sec.10.4). That divergence is a registrar item (Sec.11.6), not something this branch resolves. A retinocytomatous area does not set the code where the report states G3, G4 or severe anaplasia for the rest of the tumour: the higher grade governs (registrar's decision, 7 October 2026; contract Sec.2.4).

options.label: The entire specimen is retinocytoma/retinoma — no viable (malignant) retinoblastoma component is described anywhere in the specimen

behaviour_exclusion.reason: Retinocytoma (retinoma) is the benign counterpart of retinoblastoma. ICD-O-3.2 codes it 9510/0. ICCC-3 Group V admits behaviour 3 only, so it is not a registrable cancer in this group and no Group V code is emitted for it. Record the finding and refer the case to the registrar.
